_readme: SINGLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for the benchmark problem set. Consumed by:
judge/pairwise_evaluator.py (subject -> dist dir / html naming / problem file)
Add new problems here FIRST; nothing else needs editing for a new problem

conventions.id: kebab-or-plain slug, NO underscores (variant ids are '<id>_vN')
conventions.dist_dir: dist/<id>/  — same slug as id, no spaces (legacy entries are grandfathered)
conventions.html_naming: variant_id  — lesson files are <id>_vN.html (legacy 'bare_version' entries use vN.html)
conventions.problem_file: path relative to agentic_pipeline/ with the exact problem statement
conventions.answer: canonical final answer, phrased so equivalent forms count; put non-essential detail in parentheses marked as not required
conventions.domain: math | physics | cs — academic subject, for spread/reporting only. NOT the same thing consumers call 'subject' elsewhere (there, 'subject' means this problem's id — one problem is its own judging bucket). Adding this field does not change that.
conventions.difficulty: easy | medium | hard — informal, for reporting/spread only

problems.title: Nested Circles (AMC 10A 2023 P15)
problems.answer: 64 circles (n = 32 shaded rings, so 2n = 64)

problems.title: Archer / Projectile Range
problems.answer: approximately 141 m (141.4 m with g = 9.8 m/s^2; 138.6 m acceptable if g = 10)

problems.title: Binary Search
problems.answer: target 45 is found at index 7, and binary search runs in O(log n). (Reaching it in 4 steps is supporting detail, NOT required for a correct final answer.)

problems.title: Minimum Surface Area Box
problems.answer: base side 4 m, height 2 m, minimum surface area 48 square meters

problems.title: Simple Pendulum Period
problems.answer: period is pi seconds, approximately 3.14 s

problems.title: 0/1 Knapsack
problems.answer: items A and B (weight 5, value 7) give the maximum value of 7; solved via O(nW) dynamic programming

problems.title: Dijkstra's Shortest Path
problems.answer: shortest path S-B-A-C-T with total distance 7

problems.title: Quadratic Roots (Vieta's Formulas)
problems.answer: k = 10 (roots are 2 and 5)

problems.title: Population Standard Deviation
problems.answer: 2 (variance 4, mean 5)

problems.title: Frictionless Incline (Energy Conservation)
problems.answer: approximately 7.9 m/s (sqrt(2 * 9.8 * 3.2))

problems.title: Inelastic Collision (Momentum Conservation)
problems.answer: 2 m/s

problems.title: Series Circuit (Ohm's Law)
problems.answer: current 1 A; voltage across the 8 ohm resistor is 8 V

problems.title: Buoyancy (Archimedes' Principle)
problems.answer: 60% of the cube's height is submerged

problems.title: Merge Sort
problems.answer: [1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 9], O(n log n) time complexity
problems.note: distinct from binsearch: comparison sort vs. search on a sorted array, different complexity class — kept as separate family, not a duplicate

problems.title: Bouncing Ball Geometric Series
problems.answer: 60 meters total (12 down + two geometric series: 12 + 2*(8/(1-2/3)) = 12 + 48)

problems.title: Law of Cosines
problems.answer: sqrt(39), approximately 6.24 (c^2 = 25 + 49 - 2*5*7*cos60 = 39)

problems.title: Arrangements with a Restriction (BALLOON)
problems.answer: 900 (total 7!/(2!2!) = 1260 minus 6!/2! = 360 with the L's adjacent)

problems.title: Determinant and Infinitely Many Solutions
problems.answer: k = 6 (determinant 2k - 12 = 0 and the right-hand sides are proportional, so infinitely many solutions; any k != 6 gives a unique solution)

problems.title: Tangent Line via Derivative
problems.answer: y = 10x - 16 (slope 10 at the point (2, 4))
problems.note: calculus family adjacency: boxopt = optimization, this = tangent line, defintegral = area; three distinct techniques, kept as separate families

problems.title: Area Between Two Curves
problems.answer: 4/3 (curves meet at x = 0 and 2; integral of (2x - x^2) from 0 to 2)
problems.note: calculus family adjacency: see tangentline note

problems.title: Bayes' Theorem (Medical Test)
problems.note: probability family adjacency with cointoss: conditional probability vs binomial counting — different techniques, kept separate

problems.title: Vertical Throw from a Cliff (Quadratic)
problems.answer: 6 seconds (58.8 + 19.6t - 4.9t^2 = 0 reduces to t^2 - 4t - 12 = 0, roots 6 and -2)
problems.note: kinematics family adjacency with archer: 1D vertical throw with quadratic solve vs 2D projectile range — different techniques, kept separate

problems.title: Maximum Speed on a Flat Curve (Friction + Circular Motion)
problems.answer: approximately 19.8 m/s (v = sqrt(mu*g*r) = sqrt(0.8*9.8*50) = sqrt(392))

problems.title: Spring Launcher (Elastic Energy to Kinetic)
problems.answer: approximately 9.5 m/s (0.5*k*x^2 = 0.5*m*v^2, v = x*sqrt(k/m) = 0.15*sqrt(4000))
problems.note: energy-conservation family adjacency with incline: spring PE vs gravitational PE as the source — kept separate

problems.title: Ice Melting in Water (Latent + Specific Heat)
Ideal Gas Law
problems.answer: approximately 99,770 Pa, about 1.0 x 10^5 Pa (P = nRT/V)

problems.title: Standing Wave Harmonics on a String
problems.answer: wavelength 0.8 m (2L/3), wave speed 264 m/s (330 * 0.8)

problems.title: Thin Lens Equation
problems.answer: image at 15 cm on the far side; magnification -0.5 (inverted, half size)

problems.title: Coulomb's Law
problems.answer: approximately 0.6 N (F = k q1 q2 / r^2 = 8.99e9 * 6e-12 / 0.09)

problems.title: Hydrostatic Force on an Aquarium Window
problems.answer: approximately 616 N (P = rho*g*h = 19600 Pa at the center; F = P * pi * r^2 = 19600 * 0.0314)
problems.note: fluids family adjacency with buoyancy: pressure-force on a surface vs floating fraction — different principles, kept separate

problems.title: Topological Sort (Course Prerequisites)
problems.answer: one valid order is A, B, C, D, E; course E must always come last. (A and B may swap; any order satisfying the prerequisites is acceptable.)
problems.note: graph family adjacency with dijkstra: DAG ordering vs weighted shortest path — different algorithms, kept separate

problems.title: Cycle Detection (Floyd's Tortoise and Hare)
problems.answer: pointers first meet at node 4; the cycle starts at node 3

problems.title: Hash Table Collisions (Linear Probing)
problems.answer: 10 in slot 3, 17 in slot 4, 24 in slot 5 (all hash to 3; linear probing walks forward)

problems.title: Fibonacci with Memoization
problems.answer: F(10) = 55; memoization caches each F(k) so every subproblem is computed once (O(n) calls instead of O(2^n))
problems.note: DP family adjacency with knapsack: memoized recursion vs 0/1 table-filling — different DP styles, kept separate

problems.title: Solving Recurrences (Divide and Conquer)
problems.answer: A: T(n) = 2T(n/2) + n is O(n log n); B: T(n) = 2T(n/2) + c is O(n); B is faster for large n

problems.title: Longest Substring Without Repeats (Sliding Window)
problems.answer: 3 (the window never holds more than 'abc' / 'bca' / 'cab' — any longer window repeats a character)

problems.title: LRU Cache Eviction
problems.answer: B is evicted first (when D is inserted), then C (when B is re-inserted)

problems.title: Tower of Hanoi (4 Disks)
problems.answer: 15 moves (2^4 - 1; each added disk doubles the work plus one move)
problems.note: recursion family adjacency with fibmemo: pure recursion pattern vs memoized DP — kept separate
